Question: In the sequence \(2001,\) \(2002,\) \(2003,\) \(\ldots,\) each term after the third is found by subtracting the previous term from the sum of the two terms that precede that term. For example, the fourth term is \(2001 + 2002 - 2003 = 2000.\) What is the \(2004\)th term in this sequence?
Solution:
Let \(a_n\) denote the \(n\)th term. The first few terms are \(2001,2002,2003,2000,2005,1998\), suggesting that the even-position terms decrease by \(2\). To prove that this continues, use the recurrence twice. For every integer \(n\geq1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{n+4}
&=a_{n+1}+a_{n+2}-a_{n+3}\\
&=a_{n+1}+a_{n+2}-(a_n+a_{n+1}-a_{n+2})\\
&=2a_{n+2}-a_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(a_{n+4}-a_{n+2}=a_{n+2}-a_n\): consecutive differences within the even-position terms are equal. Since \(a_2=2002\) and \(a_4=2000\), these terms form an arithmetic sequence with common difference \(-2\).

The \(2004\)th term is the \(1002\)nd even-position term, so it is \(1001\) decreases after \(a_2\). Therefore
\[
a_{2004}=2002-2(1001)=\boxed{0},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
